title: Motion for an extension of time within which to file the briefs on the merits

pages.text:
501 WASHINGTON AVENUE
MONTGOMERY, AL 36130
(334) 242-7300
ALABAMAAG.GOV
S TA TE  OF  A L A B A M A
OFF IC E OF T HE AT TOR NEY GENER AL
STEVE MARSHALL
ATTORNEY GENERAL
June 16, 2025
Scott Harris
Clerk of the Court
Supreme Court of the United States
1 First Street, N.E.
Washington, D.C.  20543
Re: Hamm v. Smith , No. 24-872—Briefing Schedule
Dear Mr. Harris:
We write with regard to the briefing schedule in Hamm v. Smith, No. 24-872. The Court
granted certiorari in this case on June 6, 2025, and has not yet scheduled the oral argument.
The parties respectfully request 14-day extensions of time to file their merits briefs, which
would make their briefs due on the following dates:
Petitioner’s brief: August 4, 2025
Respondent’s brief: September 17, 2025.
This schedule would ensure that briefing is completed in advance of any oral argument date
for the November session or thereafter. The parties request these extensions in light of
professional obligations in other matters. For example, petitioner’s counsel have significant
briefing and oral argument obligations, including oral argument in Sharifi v. Warden, No.
24-11280 (11th Cir.), oral argument in Whatley v. Commissioner, No. 23-12863 (11th Cir.),
briefing in Washington v. Commissioner, No. 24-13905 (11th Cir.), and appellate briefing
and remedial proceedings in Singleton v. Allen, No. 21-CV-01291 (N.D. Ala.). Similarly,
respondent’s counsel has case obligations in In re State of Alabama v. David Lee Roberts,
No. 1971713 (Alabama Supreme Court) in which the State of Alabama is seeking an
execution date.
Sincerely,
s/ Edmund G. LaCour Jr.
Edmund G. LaCour Jr.
Counsel for Petitioner
s/ Kacey L. Keeton
Kacey L. Keeton
Counsel for Respondent
